title: Nothing revisits a note's Uncertainties when another note answers one
description:
From the prose review of 2026-11-26, cross-file finding.

Three design notes hedge on something a later note has since answered,
and one stated a conclusion a decision reversed. The reversed conclusion
and the stale status lines are fixed in 394d7123; the mechanism that let
them rot is not.

Cases found:

- nostr-comparison.md hedged twice on whether wn-agent's control API
  sends edits, reactions and attachments ("not traced"). marmot-bridge.md
  section 0 later traced the whole API and answers it.
- didwebvh-appdata-spike.md hedged twice on whether mls-rs supports
  AppDataUpdate. didwebvh-mls-rs.md established that stock mls-rs has
  none and that its custom-proposal API cannot carry one.
- nostr-comparison.md's conclusion was "relay mode first; puppets only
  if someone asks", which decision 12 reversed on 2026-11-21. Fixed.

Each note opens an Uncertainties section honestly. Nothing in the repo
makes anyone revisit those entries when a later note closes one, so the
oldest note keeps asking a question the newest has answered, and a
reader who starts at the wrong file gets the wrong answer.

Options, none obviously right:

- a bead per open uncertainty, closed when a note answers it. Honest but
  it is a lot of beads, and the review found 25 uncertainty entries
  across ten files.
- a convention that answering another note's uncertainty means editing
  that note in the same commit.
- accept it, and date every note's Uncertainties section so a reader
  knows how stale it is.

The second is cheapest and matches how the status-line rot happened:
the fix landed in one file and the other was not touched.
